description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:175

  pub fn register_account(&self, account_id: &Id)

The doc-comment says 'Use this in tests that need an empty-but-valid
account.' The method is test scaffolding — but it is:

- NOT marked #[doc(hidden)]
- NOT suffixed `_for_test`
- DOES NOT carry the explicit 'Production callers must not use this
  method; the API stability disclaimer on the memory feature
  applies doubly here.' banner that 5 of the 10 sibling test-only
  methods on MemoryBackend DO carry

Compare to:

  #[doc(hidden)]
  pub fn set_protect_last_admin_for_test(&self, value: bool) {...}    // memory.rs:270
  
  #[doc(hidden)]
  pub fn set_limits_for_test(&self, limits: Option<ChatLimits>) {...}  // memory.rs:352
  
  #[doc(hidden)]
  pub fn insert_object_for_test(...) {...}                             // memory.rs:367

All three carry the 'production must not use' banner and the
_for_test suffix.

Contract effect:

1. register_account appears in cargo doc output. Downstream
   consumers reading docs see it as a documented part of the
   API and write production code against it.

2. Once any downstream consumer's test suite calls
   `backend.register_account(&id)`, the maintainer cannot rename,
   remove, or change its signature without a major version bump.
   The 'memory' feature's overall 'API stability is opt-in via
   this feature and may break across minor versions' (lib.rs:25-27)
   is a written-down intent, but the workspace's behavior pattern
   on other _for_test methods shows the maintainer DOES intend
   per-method opt-out — register_account just missed it.

3. The 'memory' feature banner argues 'demonstration only' but
   register_account is a verb-shaped admin API ('register an
   account'). Production multi-tenant servers that wire identity
   middleware will reach for it on first read. The shape invites
   misuse.

Recommended fix:

  /// Test-only entry point that ... Production callers must not
  /// use this method; the API stability disclaimer on the memory
  /// feature applies doubly here.
  #[doc(hidden)]
  pub fn register_account_for_test(&self, account_id: &Id) {...}

If the public name needs to stay (compatibility with existing
in-tree integration tests), keep it but add #[doc(hidden)] + the
banner immediately. This is pre-1.0; safe to fix.

Sibling: JMAP-x2gd.45 (no test-shape macro) addresses the
backend-conformance side of the same gap. This finding addresses
the specific public-surface leak.
title: API contract: MemoryBackend::register_account is public test-scaffolding without doc(hidden) or stability banner
